The Endangered Species Act (ESA) establishes a federal program dedicated to conserving species and ecosystems that are at risk of extinction. Its primary legal implication is the imposition of a duty on federal agencies to ensure that any actions they authorize, fund, or carry out do not jeopardize the continued existence of any species listed as threatened or endangered, nor do they destroy or modify the designated critical habitat for those species. This requirement serves as a safeguard to prevent federal activities from contributing to the decline or extinction of protected wildlife and plants.
